site.name: Kicker Mine
overview: Kicker Mine was a documented tungsten mine in Boulder County's Nederland-area mining landscape, developed on a branch of the Western Star vein system.
U.S. Geological Survey records show repeated operation from the early twentieth century through the late 1920s, with the mine's largest annual output occurring during the World War I tungsten boom.

timeline.text: USGS records the Kicker Mine in operation during this period.
The mine operated again, with its strongest annual production reported during 1913-1918.
USGS records another sustained period of operation through the 1920s.
The property was worked for a shorter period again during the 1930s.

moreHistory: USGS Professional Paper 245 places the Kicker Mine at about 8,435 feet elevation, approximately 750 feet north 63 degrees east of the Western Star shaft, and documents workings on a branch of the Western Star vein system.

The same federal report describes the vein as striking about N. 60 degrees E. and dipping about 65 degrees northwest in granite, preserving useful mine-specific geologic context rather than only a place name.

A USGS-topographic/GNIS-derived mine point near 39.962765, -105.509998 provides a defensible mine-level identification anchor. Remnant does not represent that point as a field-surveyed surviving shaft or portal.
